title: Back every interlocking payload contract with a schema body

facts.note: Validation subject kind is interlocking (source validation.subject_kind).
Validation runs at CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking; covers every referenced payload contract in the interlocking, changed or unchanged.

values: artifact_reference_resolution: payload contract identity does not resolve to a contract schema body on disk
facts.note: Detector finding from the resolution validator; requires parsing interlocking messages and resolving each contract identity.

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking message references a payload contract identity whose expected schema path has no file on disk.
At CONFIRM, an interlocking message references a payload contract identity whose expected schema path exists but does not contain a contract schema body for that contract.
At CONFIRM, a long-standing, unchanged interlocking message still references a contract that resolves to no schema body.
doesNotFire: At CONFIRM, every payload contract identity referenced by interlocking messages resolves to a contract schema body on disk.
An interlocking message that references no payload contract identity (payload typing is a separate convention).

given: An interlocking whose messages reference payload contract identities (any interlocking, regardless of author or whether the reference changed).
when: The interlocking is validated at CONFIRM, where this check is confirm-blocking.
then: Ensure every payload contract identity referenced by an interlocking message resolves to a contract schema body on disk.
prefer: Plan the contract schema body at its expected schema path alongside the interlocking message that references the contract, so the reference resolves before CONFIRM.
avoid: Referencing a payload contract identity in an interlocking message that has no schema body on disk (a name-only contract).
Treating an existing file at the expected path as sufficient when it does not hold the contract's schema body.
Silencing the finding by removing or loosening the payload contract reference instead of providing the schema body.
why: An interlocking message is only a usable contract if its payload identity resolves to a concrete schema body; a dangling contract reference cannot be validated or implemented against.
evidence: For each interlocking message with a payload contract identity, the identity resolves to a contract schema body on disk at the expected schema path (file existence alone is not sufficient).
The resolution validator reports no findings at CONFIRM; any failure names interlocking_id, message_id, contract and expected_schema_path.
verifier_detail: Validation family: resolution; template: artifact_reference_resolution; variant: planner_train_interlocking_payload_contract_body_required.
Subject kind: interlocking. Runs in phase CONFIRM with enforcement confirm-blocking; checks all referenced payload contracts, not only changed ones.
Failure evidence fields: interlocking_id, message_id, contract, expected_schema_path.
Term contract_body: a payload contract identity must resolve to a contract schema body on disk.
audit: Source name: Interlocking payload contract body required

additions.text: Treating an existing file as sufficient; silencing the finding by removing/loosening the reference.
additions.justification: Anti-patterns required by the format; derived from 'resolve to a contract schema body on disk'; no new requirement.

additions.text: Engineering reason for requiring resolvable schema bodies.
additions.justification: Source has no explicit rationale; derived from the statement and the graph edge to the payload-typed convention.
